binders: ι is an arbitrary finite type; no nonemptiness assumption is made.
Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
X is an arbitrary indexed family of functions X(i) : Ω → ℝ.
λ is an arbitrary real number.
a is an arbitrary real coefficient family indexed by ι.
hypotheses: The family of real-valued functions (X(i)) indexed by ι is jointly independent with respect to μ, with Real carrying its Borel measurable structure.
For every i ∈ ι, the function ω ↦ exp(λ a(i) X(i,ω)) is integrable with respect to μ.
conclusions: The μ-integral of ω ↦ exp(λ Σ_{i∈ι} a(i)X(i,ω)) equals the finite product over i ∈ ι of the μ-integrals of ω ↦ exp(λ a(i)X(i,ω)).
mathematical_definitions: For each i, define M_i = ∫_Ω exp(λ a(i)X(i,ω)) dμ(ω).
Since μ is a probability measure, these integrals can equivalently be written as expectations: E_μ[exp(λS)] and E_μ[exp(λa(i)X(i))].
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of jointly independent real-valued functions X(i) on a probability space, any real parameter λ, and any real coefficients a(i), if each individual exponential exp(λ a(i)X(i)) is integrable, then the exponential moment of their weighted sum factors as the product of the individual exponential moments: ∫ exp(λ Σ_i a(i)X(i)) dμ = ∏_i ∫ exp(λ a(i)X(i)) dμ.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is finite, but it need not be nonempty. For an empty index type, the sum is 0, the left integrand is exp(0)=1, and the product is 1; the probability-measure assumption makes the equality reduce to 1=1.
No sign, positivity, nonzero, normalization, or boundedness restriction is imposed on λ or on the coefficients a(i).
No identical-distribution, centering, variance, boundedness, or moment assumptions on the X(i) are encoded.

The only explicit integrability assumptions concern exp(λ a(i)X(i)) at the single chosen λ and coefficient family; integrability of X(i) itself or exponential integrability on a neighborhood of λ is not required.

There is no separate explicit hypothesis that the exponential of the full weighted sum is integrable, and the conclusion is only an equality of integrals rather than a standalone assertion of that integrability.

There is no separate explicit Measurable declaration for each X(i) in the target; any such content must come from the precise iIndepFun predicate, while Integrable directly supplies almost-everywhere strong measurability only for the corresponding exponential integrands.
The result concerns one fixed probability measure μ and uses the Borel measurable structure on Real.
ambiguities: The packet defines iIndepFun only through ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.iIndepFun but does not unfold that kernel predicate, so its exact event-level formulation and whether it separately entails measurability of each X(i) cannot be reconstructed from the packet alone.

The displayed body of MeasureTheory.integral is an opaque wrapper projection, so the packet alone does not expose Lean's convention for the integral of a non-integrable function; this matters syntactically because the target does not separately assume integrability of the left-hand integrand.
